authorized_by: parent T76 explicitly confirmed before new GPU winners are available
common_constraints: PP=1, no SP, same checkpoint/recomputation/precision, same public requests and FIFO ownership convention
pass_1: Preserve GPU train_tp and rollout_tp exactly. Only decrease train_mb/logprob_mb/cap, never increase them. Enumerate feasible candidates by minimum total log2 reduction from GPU knobs.
pass_1_tie: Fixed tuple (-train_mb, -logprob_mb, -cap), ascending. This preserves training microbatch, then logprob microbatch, then cap on an equal total reduction; no timing is inspected.
pass_2: Only if no pass_1 candidate passes capacity, permit TP changes. Minimize abs(log2(train_tp/GPU_train_tp))+abs(log2(rollout_tp/GPU_rollout_tp)), then total knob log2 reduction.
pass_2_tie: Fixed tuple (train_tp, rollout_tp, -train_mb, -logprob_mb, -cap), ascending; no timing is inspected.
admission: Operators.admission over tune/test1/test2/test3/test4 declared phase memory bounds, plus integer/head/FFN/vocab/group legality. Test timing is never used. Rollout reserves max prompt +8192 independently of future response lengths; training lengths are available after rollout.
failure: If no candidate passes, report unsupported under the declared hardware; never expand memory, reduce workload/precision, or discard long requests to force a pair.
old_rule_difference: Frozen T58 first shrank phase-failing knobs iteratively, then used wafer tune latency to break equal nearest-TP ties. T76C replaces that final timing tie with a deterministic capacity-only ordering. It may also avoid unnecessary simultaneous knob reductions.
scope: A migrated GPU schedule with minimum declared capacity adjustment. It is neither a WSC-specific search optimum nor DynaRL reproduction. All WSC scheduling methods must use the same low-level cost backend.
